source.section: PDF p.15 Line 14 (the amount reported on Form 1040 line 5b, not limited to federal taxable income); Form ND-1 line 18 'If less than zero, enter 0'; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = military retirement (person 0) 30,000.00 = 30,000.00. Federal taxable income = 30,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 12,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 12,250.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 12,250.00. Subtractions: line 14 military retirement benefit exclusion 30,000.00. Line 17 total subtractions = 30,000.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 12,250.00 - 30,000.00 = -17,750.00, less than zero, so enter 0 (expected 0.00). Line 19 = 0.00. Line 20 tax: 0.00 is in the 0% band (up to 48,475.00), so the tax = 0.00. Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: not a joint return, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 0.00. The full 30,000.00 is entered on line 14 even though the federal standard deduction already took 17,750.00 of it: the line asks for the amount on Form 1040 line 5b. relief_amounts shows that full figure.
